2. Facts relevant for disposal of the Rule are that the opposite party No.1 instituted Title Suit No.249 of 1984 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Kurigram for declaration of title on correction of record of right. Plaintiff's case in short is that the suit land originally belonged to Ibrahim Sheikh and Ishaque Sheikh in equal 8 annas share. Ibrahim Sheikh died leaving two sons Azizur Rahman and Insar Ali who inherited him. Ishaque Sheikh died leaving only son Nizamuddin who inherited 8 annas share of his father in the suit property. Nizamuddin died leaving wife Habija Bewa and daughter Hasina Banu. During possession they sold 4.49 decimals of land to Alauddin vide registered kabala dated 08.01.1948. In his turn Alauddin transferred 3.17 decimals of land to the plaintiff vide registered patta taking salami of taka 970/-. Since then the plaintiff is in possession of tfiElliand7Due to illness the plaintiff could not appear before the settlement employees during last survey and as such S.A. Khatian No.64 wrongly 4 recorded in the name of defendants. Plaintiff came to know about the wrong recording when he went to pay rent to the Tahasil office. Hence, the present suit. 

 3. Defendant Nos.1-3 contested the suit by filing a joint written statement denying material allegations made in the plaint and contending inter alia that their father purchased 4.49 decimals of land from Habiza Bewa and others vide registered kabala dated 08.01.1948 and subsequently settled the land to the plaintiff. Plaintiff surrendered the land in 13.60 B.S. by giving ishtafanama being unable to pay rent. Since then the defendants are in possession of the suit land and S.A. Khatian prepared accordingly. Plaintiff has no title and possession over the suit land. With such averments they prayed for dismissal of the suit. 

 4. During pendency of the Rule the opposite party Nos.3-6 added themselves in the instant civil revision by filing an application under Order 1 Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The case of the added opposite parties are that the suit jote appertaining to C.S. Khatian No.76 measuring an area of 8.45 acres was originally belonged to Ibrahim Sheikh and Ehsan in equal 8 annas share. While possessing his 8 annas share ( Ibrahim died leaving wife Gendi Bewa, two sons Azizar Rahman and Ensar Ali and one daughter Buri Khatun. Thereafter Ehsan died leaving only son Abul Kashem. Abul Kashed died leaving two sons Solaiman All and Bablu Miah and one daughter Aklima Khatun. Azizar Rahman, one of the son of late Ibrahim Sheikh, died unmarried. Then Gendi Bewa died leaving one son Ensar Ali and one daughter Buri Khatun. Ensar Ali and Burl Khatun have been possessing 8 annas share of the suit jote left by their father Ibrahim Sheikh. 8 annas share of Ehsan now under the possession of his two sons and one daughter Solaiman, Bablu and Aklima Khatun. Nizamuddin son of Arabuddin Mohammad had no interest in the suit jote and had no title and possession over the suit jote. From C.S. Khatian No.10 of Mouza Dakkhin Basjani, it is apparent that Nizamuddin Munshi, Ehsanuddin Sheikh, Ibrahim Sheikh, Zahiruddin Sarkar and Jonab Uddin Sarkar are the sons of Arabuddin Mohammad and Nizamuddin 'was not the son of Ehsanuddin. Kabala of the plaintiff is fraudulent and collusive. The heirs of C.S. tenant Ibrahim Sheikh" and Ehsan are now possessing the suit land and the opposite party. Nos.3-6 have been possessing their respective share along with the heirs of Ehsan but' those persons were not made parties. 

 5. At the time of hearing of the Rule, learned Advocate for the petitioners filed an application under Order 41 Rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure for producing two rent receipts of Khatian No.64 of the suit land as additional evidence before this court. It is stated in the application that father of this applicant late Rafigul Hoque defendant witness No.1 made his deposition before the trial court and at the time he handed over the rent receipts of Khatian No.64 to his learned Advocate for submitting in the court but the learned Advocate inadvertently did not submit the documents in the court for which the rent receipts has not been marked as Exhibits in the case record. It is stated in the application that the learned Advocate inadvertently did-not submit the rent receipts in the trial court but it appears that the defendant-petitioners did not take any step to file the rent receipts in the appellate court below though they had ample opportunity to produce the same before the appellate court below. The provisions of order 41 rule 27 are clearly not intended to allow a litigant who has been unsuccessful in the lower court to patch up the weak parts of his case and fill up the omissions in the revisional court and as such the application for additional evidence is not necessary at this point of time to pronounce judgment. 

 11. It appears that both the parties admits that Alauddin, predecessor of the defendants, settled the suit land to the plaintiff vide registered patta. Discord between the parties started thereafter. Plaintiff claims that he took settlement of the land vide registered patta and since then he is in possession of the suit land. He further claims that due to illness the plaintiff could not appear before the settlement employees during last survey and as such S.A. Khatian No.64 wrongly recorded in the name of defendants and he came to know about the wrong recording when he went to pay rent to the Tahasil Office. On the other hand the definite case of the defendant Nos.1-3 is that plaintiff surrendered the suit land in 1360 B.S. by giving ishtafanama being unable to pay rent and since then the defendants are in possession of the suit land. S.A. Khatian prepared accordingly. I have carefully and meticulously gone through the judgment passed by the courts below. It appears that the learned Assistant Judge after framing proper issues and after threadbare discussions on the issues arrived at a finding : 

 12. The plaintiff has filed the suit for declaration of title on assertion that he is in possession of the suit land and the recording of S.A. Khatian No.64 is wrong. Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act provides that a suit for mere declaration of any legal character or any right to property is maintainable. In view of the evidence of possession in favour of the plaintiff, the plaintiff need not ask for any further relief. In view of the matter, I am of the opinion that present suit for mere declaration is maintainable.
